shotCard.focus: an old railway conductor quietly checks a small weathered folded train pass offered by the black leather-gloved hand of an unidentified traveler across a polished wooden compartment table
shotCard.camera: tight close-up within a vintage passenger compartment focused on the pass between the conductor's hands and the unseen traveler's one gloved hand, the faces and bodies out of frame
shotCard.location: a traditional wooden passenger railway carriage in industrial Birmingham in the 1920s
required: one old railway conductor's two bare weathered hands carefully holding a small folded period train pass with indistinct markings
one black leather-gloved anonymous traveler's hand touching the offered pass over a dark wooden carriage table
one warm brass oil lamp and rain-streaked railway carriage window showing smoke-darkened brick factory buildings at dawn
shotCard.background: dark tufted leather carriage seat, wooden wall panels, brass fittings, a leather-bound folio and an old pocket watch on the narrow table
shotCard.light: warm amber oil lamp on weathered hands and paper against cold misty industrial sunrise through the rain-covered carriage window
shotCard.npc: the conductor is seen only by uniformed sleeves, torso and bare hands; the anonymous traveler by one gloved hand, without identifiable faces or physique
shotCard.knowledgeBoundary: The ticket inspection is compatible with one or more independently recorded evacuated-witness states. It does not establish which witnesses boarded, how many travelers are elsewhere in the carriage, or whether they arrived safely. The unaccompanied-departure state remains a separate scene, and game status is determined only by witness flags.
avoid: a full recognizable playable hero body or face, or an invented face for Ada, Tommy or Mercer
multiple identifiable witnesses implying that all three were evacuated together
legible passenger names, new identities, private addresses or guaranteed safe-arrival stamp
celebration, arrival at a protected destination, or a conclusive resolution of all witness fates
